Title: WHAT'S IN THE TUBE?

AnswerDetails: Real answer: a safety hood ("breathing device") whose long tube draws cleaner air from near the ground, patented by Garrett A. Morgan, 1914 (US patent 1,113,675). RealAnswer: A safety hood for breathing in smoke or fumes, its long tube drawing cleaner air from near the floor

RealAnswer: A desk that folds out into a full-size bed

RealAnswer: The ice-cream scoop: squeeze the handle and a scraper frees a neat ball from the cone-shaped mould

AnswerDetails: Real answer: a combined rocking chair and fan, the rocking motion working a fan above the sitter, patented by C. Horst, 1847 (US patent 5,231). The arm curving over the chair carries a fan blade driven by the chair itself, so the harder you rock, the cooler you get.
RealAnswer: A rocking chair that works a fan over your head as you rock

Title: A CHAIR THAT WANTS ATTENTION
CustomInstruction: What does this invention do? Give it your best guess: accurate, absurd or brilliant.
AnswerDetails: Real answer: the "gong and signal chair for hotels": press a button and a gong sounds and a signal shows which seat wants service, patented by Miriam E. Title: BELLOWS ON A BOAT?

AnswerDetails: Real answer: a "double bicycle for looping the loop", with wheels above the rider for the upside-down part of a loop track, patented by Karl Lange, 1905 (US patent 790,063). Title: A BRUSH FOR THE VIEW

AnswerDetails: Real answer: the windscreen wiper ("window-cleaning device"), worked by a lever from inside the vehicle, patented by Mary Anderson, 1903 (US patent 743,801). RealAnswer: Spectacles for chickens, to protect their eyes from being pecked by other chickens

Title: WINGS AND GEARS

RealAnswer: A tiny timer camera strapped to a carrier pigeon's chest, taking aerial photos in flight

Title: HOLD STILL, BESSIE

AnswerDetails: Real answer: a cow-tail holder, clamping the tail to the leg during milking, patented by James M. Worden, 1875 (US patent 159,490). Anyone who has milked by hand knows the problem: a cow's tail swatting flies tends to land on the milker. This strap and clamp kept it out of the way.
RealAnswer: A clamp that holds a cow's tail to her leg, so she cannot swish it in the milker's face

Title: A WHEEL FOR A WORKER

AnswerDetails: Real answer: a "dog-power", a tilted treadwheel a dog walks on to drive small machinery such as a butter churn, patented by David E. Pangburn, 1874 (US patent 154,075). RealAnswer: A dog-powered treadwheel: the dog walks on the tilted wheel and turns a shaft that can run small farm machines

RealAnswer: The Landlord's Game, the board game that became Monopoly
